title: Lubricating Oil Skid
model_title: Lubricating Oil Skid (Pressure-Fed, API 614 style) for a Turbomachine

introduction.definition: A lubricating oil skid supplies clean, cool oil at controlled pressure to the bearings of a turbine, compressor or large pump. Main and standby pumps draw from a heated reservoir, coolers and duplex filters condition the oil, a pressure-control valve spills excess back, and an accumulator bridges pump switch-over.
key_points: Standby pump auto-starts on low pressure
introduction.summary: A lubricating oil skid supplies clean, cool oil at controlled pressure to the bearings (and often seals and controls) of a turbine, compressor or large pump, with main and standby pumps, coolers, duplex filters and a reservoir.

pressure.title: Clean, cool oil at controlled pressure
pressure.description: The main pump delivers more oil than the machine needs; the pressure-control valve spills the excess back to the reservoir to hold header pressure (typically ≈ 1–2.5 bar(g) at the bearings). Coolers keep supply ≈ 40–50 °C; duplex filters (≈ 10 µm) can be switched on-line. The standby pump starts automatically on falling pressure, and the accumulator / rundown tank covers the switch-over and coast-down so bearings are never starved.

foundation: Skid / unit on a level, rigid base; anchor bolts; accessible for maintenance.
alignment: Align pump-motor drives; level reservoirs and headers; slope drain lines as specified.
piping: Pickle / flush lube piping to the cleanliness target before connecting to bearings; avoid low pockets in mist/grease lines.

video_tutorials.title: Lubricating Oil Skid — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Lubricating Oil Skid.
A lubricating oil skid supplies clean, cool oil at controlled pressure to the bearings of a turbine, compressor or large pump.
Main and standby pumps draw from a heated reservoir, coolers and duplex filters condition the oil, a pressure-control valve spills excess back, and an accumulator bridges pump switch-over.
Typical applications include turbo-compressors, steam and gas turbines; large pumps, gearboxes and generators.

The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Main Lube Oil Pump, Main Lube Oil Pump — Shaft & Coupling (turning), Standby (auto-start on low pressure) Lube Oil Pump, Standby (auto-start on low pressure) Lube Oil Pump — Shaft & Coupling (turning).
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Lubricating Oil Skid — Operation

script.narration: How the Lubricating Oil Skid works.
The main pump draws oil from the reservoir.
Coolers remove bearing heat.
Duplex filters clean the oil.
The PCV holds header pressure.
Oil returns to the reservoir.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.
The main pump delivers more oil than the machine needs; the pressure-control valve spills the excess back to the reservoir to hold header pressure (typically ≈ 1–2.5 bar(g) at the bearings).

video_tutorials.title: Lubricating Oil Skid — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Lubricating Oil Skid.
Check pressures, temperatures, filter ΔP, level.
Oil analysis; test standby auto-start.
Clean reservoir; service pumps/coolers.
Watch for low oil pressure trip: machine trips. Common cause: filter blocked, pcv fault, pump failure.
Watch for water in oil: milky oil. Common cause: cooler leak, seal steam.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
